findings.topic: Lock order, retirement and failure profile
findings.source: io_memory.cpp Impl::Access/Mutation/Call; close/destructor and SDK wrappers
findings.observation: Parent Operation is validated before IO gate acquisition; no nested parent Operation opens. Reentrant raw allocation/free is guarded. Close rejects records/active calls/poison, enters Retiring and releases provider lease outside IO gate; Closed is mandatory for destruction. Once parent allocation/free was attempted, ANY thrown result, including known bad_alloc/HeapFreeFALSE, poisons IO and retains record; native callback exceptions likewise poison. There is no IO reset/recovery or automatic retry, even if parent raw-only retry later reclaims storage. Unknown SDK throw retains pending sidecar/range/extra owner; own child exits with retained state rather than inventing rollback.
